Input Formats, Replicates and Normalization

Maria K. Janowska

2026-11-05

Source: vignettes/input_formats.Rmd
input_formats.Rmd

This vignette shows how to load data, how replicates are handled, and which value scales are available.

library(HDXBoxeR)

Reading data

Every function that takes filepath also takes a table that is already loaded. Load the data once with read_hdx() and pass it on.

HDXExaminer

Export from HDXExaminer: Tools > Export > All results table (see ?All_results_table).

f3 <- system.file("extdata", "three_states.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
d3 <- read_hdx(f3)
table(d3$Protein.State, d3$Deut.Time)
#>              
#>                0s 1800.00s 4.00s 60.00s  FD
#>   D109H_pH7.5 150      200   150    200  85
#>   R120G_ph7.5  99      198   150    150  75
#>   WT_pH7.5    149      200   200    200 132

Waters DynamX

read_hdx() also reads DynamX cluster data and state data (DynamX 2.x and 3.x).

  • Cluster data: each raw file is one replicate. Uptake is calculated from the centroid mass.
  • State data: one average value per peptide, without replicates. It can be plotted, but the significance tests need cluster data.
  • DynamX exposure times (minutes) become seconds: 0.5 min is "30.00s".
d <- read_hdx("cluster_data.csv",
              fd = "Full Deuteration control",  # state with the FD control, or "last"
              combine_charges = FALSE)          # TRUE merges charge states

Other software

as_hdx_long() takes a table with one row per measurement. Name the columns that hold each value:

long <- data.frame(state = rep(c("apo", "holo"), each = 6),
                   t_min = rep(rep(c(1, 10), each = 3), 2),
                   run = rep(paste0("r", 1:3), 4),
                   from = 5, to = 14, seq = "YIAKQRPISF",
                   D = c(1.1, 1.2, 1.15, 2.4, 2.5, 2.45, 0.9, 1.0, 0.95, 2.0, 2.1, 2.05))
d_long <- as_hdx_long(long, state = "state", time = "t_min", replicate = "run",
                      start = "from", end = "to", sequence = "seq", uptake = "D",
                      time_unit = "min")
output_tp(d_long)
#> Protein.States used: apo holo
#> Deut.times used: 60.00s 600.00s
#> Number of replicates used: apo=3 holo=3
#> no csv file written
#>   Deut.Time Start End   Sequence Search.RT Charge apo_X..Deut_1 apo_X..Deut_2
#> 1    60.00s     5  14 YIAKQRPISF         0      1           1.1           1.2
#> 2   600.00s     5  14 YIAKQRPISF         0      1           2.4           2.5
#>   apo_X..Deut_3 holo_X..Deut_1 holo_X..Deut_2 holo_X..Deut_3
#> 1          1.15            0.9            1.0           0.95
#> 2          2.45            2.0            2.1           2.05

Replicates

All replicates are used, and states can have different numbers of replicates. In three_states.csv the wild type has 4 replicates; the mutants have 3 or 4, depending on the peptide. The table has one column per replicate (4 per state here), and a missing replicate is NA.

a3 <- output_tp(d3)
#> Protein.States used: WT_pH7.5 D109H_pH7.5 R120G_ph7.5
#> Deut.times used: 4.00s 60.00s 1800.00s
#> 66 peptide row(s) dropped: 66 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: WT_pH7.5=4 D109H_pH7.5=4 R120G_ph7.5=4
#> no csv file written
attr(a3, "replicates")
#>    WT_pH7.5 D109H_pH7.5 R120G_ph7.5 
#>           4           4           4
## replicates with a value, per state, for the first peptides
sapply(c("WT", "D109H", "R120G"), function(s) rowSums(!is.na(a3[1:5, grep(s, colnames(a3))])))
#>   WT D109H R120G
#> 1  4     3     3
#> 2  4     3     3
#> 3  4     3     3
#> 4  4     3     3
#> 5  4     3     3
  • A peptide is used when it has at least 2 replicates in every state (min_replicates). Dropped peptides are reported.
  • replicates = 3 uses at most 3 replicates per state.

Point mutants

Peptides covering a mutation have a different sequence in the mutant. By default only peptides with the same sequence are compared. seq_match = TRUE matches peptides by position, so these peptides are kept:

by_seq <- output_tp(d3, times = "60.00s")
#> Protein.States used: WT_pH7.5 D109H_pH7.5 R120G_ph7.5
#> 22 peptide row(s) dropped: 22 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: WT_pH7.5=4 D109H_pH7.5=4 R120G_ph7.5=3
#> no csv file written
by_pos <- output_tp(d3, times = "60.00s", seq_match = TRUE)
#> Protein.States used: WT_pH7.5 D109H_pH7.5 R120G_ph7.5
#> Number of replicates used: WT_pH7.5=4 D109H_pH7.5=4 R120G_ph7.5=3
#> no csv file written
c(by_sequence = nrow(by_seq), by_position = nrow(by_pos))
#> by_sequence by_position 
#>          40          50

compare_states_tp() and compare_regions() do the same with by = "position".

Value scales

percent sets the values used everywhere:

percent Values
FALSE (default) uptake in Da
TRUE percent deuteration from the input (HDXExaminer Deut %)
"per_residue" uptake per exchangeable residue (Da / nb_exch_deut())
"FD" percent of the fully deuterated control

Long peptides take up more deuterium in Da than short ones. TRUE, "per_residue" and "FD" remove this, so peptide length does not affect the result. "FD" also corrects for back-exchange. p-values are the same on every scale.

a_fd <- output_tp(d3, times = "60.00s", percent = "FD")
#> Protein.States used: WT_pH7.5 D109H_pH7.5 R120G_ph7.5
#> 22 peptide row(s) dropped: 22 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: WT_pH7.5=4 D109H_pH7.5=4 R120G_ph7.5=3
#> no csv file written
summary(unlist(a_fd[, 7:ncol(a_fd)]))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   27.12   57.00   74.59   70.70   86.24  105.68

With "FD", peptides without an FD value stay in the table with NA.

Peptide checks

peptide_qc() flags missing controls, uptake of 0 at every time point, negative uptake, and odd FD values. It does not remove anything.

qc <- peptide_qc(d3)
qc[qc$issues != "", c("Protein.State", "Start", "End", "issues")]
#> [1] Protein.State Start         End           issues       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

How this connects to the rest of the package

After loading Use
Check the data peptide_qc(), general_info(), plot_peptide_coverage_map() (vignette("data_quality"))
Organize for analysis output_tp() (time points), output_tc() (time courses)
Compare two states plot_fissure_vent() and the plots in vignette("HDXBoxeR")
Compare more states, regions, time courses compare_states_tp(), compare_regions(), compare_timecourse() (vignette("multistate"))
Report hdx_summary_table(), hdx_results_table(), render_report()
